themes_detail.label: Animal Abuse Spike in Belmont
themes_detail.summary: Animal abuse complaints surged to 15 last week versus a baseline average of 2.1 per week (606% increase, z-score 7.3), signaling a potential coordinated animal welfare crisis or reporting surge in CD 206 this week.
evidence: 15 animal abuse complaints last week vs. 2.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (606% spike, z-score 7.3)
Coincides with elevated dead animal complaints (10 last week vs. 1.0 avg, 900% spike)
Suggests possible pattern: animal cruelty incidents, neglect cases, or organized fighting activity
reporting_angles: Interview ASPCA/local animal rescues about whether they've fielded uptick in Belmont complaints or cases
Investigate whether complaints cluster by location (park, specific blocks, residential areas) suggesting targeted incidents
Report on resident safety concerns if animal abuse is linked to gang activity or neighborhood instability

themes_detail.label: Dead Animals Accumulating Rapidly
themes_detail.summary: Dead animal complaints hit 10 last week, up 900% from the 1.0-per-week baseline (z-score 9.0), suggesting possible disease outbreak, poor sanitation infrastructure, or pest control failure in CD 206 this week.
evidence: 10 dead animal complaints last week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (900% spike, z-score 9.0)
Clusters with elevated animal-in-park complaints (4 two weeks ago vs. 0.2 avg) and animal abuse spike
Public health concern: dead animals attract rodents and may indicate broader sanitation or wildlife management failure
reporting_angles: Contact DSNY and Parks Dept to ask if they've identified source (overflowing sanitation, illegal dumping, rabid animal outbreak)
Investigate whether dead animals are concentrated in specific parks or streets—suggests targeted problem area
Report on health department response and whether residents are being advised of disease risk (rabies, toxoplasmosis)

themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Crisis Emerging
themes_detail.summary: Street light complaints jumped to 14 last week, up 229% from a 4.2-per-week baseline (z-score 3.84), indicating potential widespread infrastructure failure or negligent maintenance in CD 206 this week, with direct safety and quality-of-life impact.
evidence: 14 street light complaints last week vs. 4.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (229% spike, z-score 3.84)
Long-running community board ask for 'other transportation infrastructure' suggests street lighting has been neglected for years
Dark streets correlate with elevated safety concerns; timing coincides with other spikes (graffiti, encampments, obstruction)
reporting_angles: File FOIL request for Con Edison outage logs and DOT maintenance schedules in CD 206 for past 4 weeks
Canvass residents on which streets are darkest; interview safety advocates about correlation with crime or encampments
Report on city's response timeline: how long does DSNY/DOT typically take to address street light failures?

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion in Belmont
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints exploded to 16 three weeks ago, up 967% from a 1.5-per-week baseline (z-score 12.97), the largest statistical anomaly in the data, suggesting possible gang territorial marking, inadequate removal enforcement, or coordinated vandalism campaign in early December.
evidence: 16 graffiti complaints three weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (967% spike, z-score 12.97—highest z-score in dataset)
Highest statistical severity of any complaint type, but timing is 3 weeks old—not THIS WEEK but notable for persistence
May indicate gang activity, tag wars, or failure of city graffiti removal program
reporting_angles: Interview NYPD about whether 16th or 41st precinct has gang intelligence linking spike to territorial activity
Check with DSNY on graffiti removal response times and budgets in CD 206 vs. other Bronx districts
Photograph tagged areas to document whether graffiti has persisted three weeks later (indicates slow removal)

themes_detail.label: Encampment Growth Suspected
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints jumped to 5 three weeks ago, up 344% from a 1.1-per-week baseline (z-score 3.05), suggesting possible homeless population surge or ineffective outreach coordination in CD 206 in early December.
evidence: 5 encampment complaints three weeks ago vs. 1.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (344% spike, z-score 3.05)
Correlates with elevated obstruction complaints (4 last week vs. 0.9 avg, 357% spike) and street light failures, suggesting environmental deterioration
Community board has never requested dedicated homeless services or shelter expansion—suggests issue may be under-recognized by leadership
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 5 encampment complaints to identify whether they cluster (e.g., near parks, transit hubs, abandoned buildings)
Interview DHS outreach teams on whether they've increased engagement in CD 206 in past month
Report on resident sentiment: are encampments driving other quality-of-life complaints (graffiti, dead animals, obstruction)?
